mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST decreases > 10%, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5%, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following two consecutive months of RSAFS increase, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
